## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sirikāḷakaṇṇijātaka* (Ja 382) is a tale from the Pali Jātaka collection. The framing story opens at the Jetavana monastery concerning the wealthy merchant Anāthapiṇḍika [Fausböll 1883]. Following his attainment of stream-entry (*sotāpatti*), Anāthapiṇḍika and his entire household—including his wife, children, servants, and laborers—strictly observed the five moral precepts and kept the Sabbath (*uposatha*) days [Nyanaponika, Hecker, and Bodhi 2003; Fausböll 1883]. When the monks gathered in the Dhammasabhā discussed the exceptional moral conduct of Anāthapiṇḍika's household, the Buddha recounted an old tale demonstrating that wise householders in the past also fostered virtuous households.

In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as a virtuous merchant householder [Anandajoti 2010; Shaw 2006]. The narrative features two goddesses—Sirī (Lakṣmī) and Kāḷakaṇṇī, personifying Fortune and Misfortune—who contest precedence to recline upon his couch [Anandajoti 2010]. Appearing in radiant golden light, Lakṣmī explains that she bestows her favor on persons who are dutiful, generous, gentle, honest, and humble, but abandons those corrupted by pride and conceit [Shaw 2006]. The verses, opening with the incipit *Kā nu kāḷena vaṇṇenā*, emphasize that lasting happiness cannot easily be won by those who commit wrong deeds [Anandajoti 2010; Fausböll 1883].

Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reveals 28 Pali-internal correspondences, predominantly with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (21 matches in the third volume and seven in the sixth volume) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns segments automatically with the Tibetan translations of the *Surataparipṛcchā-sūtra* (D0071) and the *Vikurvāṇarājaparipṛcchā-sūtra* (D0167), though these are machine matches rather than verified direct parallels [DharmaNexus].
